target: B: Clay Volume, Lithology & Basic Log Analysis - Interactive Petrophysics 2018 (PGL / Lloyd's Register / Geoactive) decompiled CHM help

raster_verdict.question: Are the Larionov / Clavier / Stieber coefficients recoverable as text?
raster_verdict.answer: NO - lost to raster. All six GR Vcl forms, plus SP, Neutron, Resistivity, Other-Linear and all four double-indicator forms, are rasterized GIFs on clayequationsandmethodology.htm (equation_images: 16). Only method labels and surrounding prose survive as text.
what_survives_as_text: Curved-method branch thresholds 0.55 and 0.73, and the identity branch VclGr = Z for 0.73 < Z < 1.0
Resistivity branch condition: Rt greater than 2 x Rclay
The entire organic-shale correction set (GrCorr / NeuCorr / DenCorr) written longhand
U = Pef x (RHOB + 0.1883) x 0.93423; Ct = 1000 / Rt; Cxo = 1000 / Rxo; Caliper = DCal + Bit Size; Velocity = 1 / DT; HI_Gas = 2.25 * GasDensity
raster_verdict.gif_files_exist_on_disk_for_human_inspec: C:\Users\ARUNIKA\AppData\Local\Temp\c18\embim23.gif .. embim38.gif (clay chain); embim14.gif .. embim22.gif (Basic Log Analysis); embim5.gif .. embim13.gif (Basic Log Functions)

methods.equation: TEXT (recoverable): 'The Minimum Clay Volume ( VCL ) curve is calculated as the minimum clay volume response of all selected single and double clay indicators, and, by default is picked as the Wet Clay Volume ( VWCL ) curve used in the set up of the Porosity and Water Saturation Module.'

methods.name: VCLAV (Average of indicators) - Mean | Median | Lateral
methods.tier: A (Lateral variant carries a Tier-B citation)

parameters.name: VCLAV method
parameters.default: not stated in manual; 'Currently the VCL Average is the mean value of all the VCL results at a level' implies Mean is the incumbent behaviour
parameters.note: 'The two new methods are ?Median? and ?Lateral?.'

methods.equation: TEXT (recoverable): Mean = mean of all VCL results at a level. Lateral = 'the median value of all the individual pair products'; expanded on curve_average.htm as 'creating pair products of the input data and then taking the median of the results.'
methods.citation: Lateral: 'This is almost identical to the Hodges-Lehmann method (J.L Hodges and E. L Lehmann, Basic Concepts of Probability and Statistics, Holden-Day 1970).' (page: curve_average.htm) - the ONLY full primary citation in the entire clay chain.
caveats: CLIPPING ORDER IS STATED AND MATTERS: 'For the VCLAV curve, the separate Vclay indicator curves will first be clipped before the average curve is created.'
Rationale for Lateral: 'it gives a median-type average that will not be badly skewed by any outliers in the data.'

methods.name: Percentile-driven endpoint picking (Gr Clean / Gr Clay from percentiles)

parameters.name: Use Percentiles
parameters.note: index (55). Two-way binding: ON -> percentiles drive Gr Clean/Gr Clay; OFF -> Gr Clean/Gr Clay drive the displayed percentiles.

parameters.name: Percentile Clean
parameters.note: index (56) - the heading is missing from the decompiled clayparameters.htm text but the body paragraph survives; described in full on basicloganalysis.htm. 'Numbers can be less than 0%. Negative percentiles are calculated by a linear scaling from the 0% to the 100% percentiles and extrapolating to the negative entered number.' Illustrative example uses a 10th percentile.

parameters.name: Percentile Clay
parameters.note: index (57). VERBATIM: 'Numbers greater than 100% are allowed and are normal for the calculation of clay volume (default is 130%). Percentiles over 100% are calculated by a linear scaling from the 0% to the 100% percentiles and extrapolating to the entered number.' Illustrative example uses a 90th percentile.

parameters.name: Percentile Group
parameters.note: index (58). 'GammRay data from Zones with the same group number are lumped together when calculating or looking up percentiles.'

parameters.name: Clip Low %
parameters.default: 0% per clayparameters.htm; 98% per basicloganalysis.htm - THE TWO PAGES CONFLICT
parameters.note: index (59). 'Enter a low clip values between 0-100%.'

parameters.name: Clip High %
parameters.default: 98% per clayparameters.htm; not stated on basicloganalysis.htm
parameters.note: index (60). 'Enter a high clip values between 0-100%.'

methods.equation: TEXT (recoverable) - the pipeline: pool GR data by Percentile Group -> clip with Clip Low % / Clip High % -> compute percentile -> linearly extrapolate beyond the 0%-100% range for percentiles outside 0-100 -> result is Gr Clean / Gr Clay.
caveats: CLIP-BEFORE-PERCENTILE ORDER IS STATED: 'The GammaRay curve data for each Percentile Group is clipped using the Clip Low % and the Clip High % parameters before the percentiles are calculated.'
UNRESOLVED CONFLICT on Clip Low % default (0% vs 98%). Do not silently pick one.

Derivation method given: crossplot (Normal Gr - Uranium-corrected Gr) vs volume TOC, linear regression, extrapolate to 100% TOC. parameters.name: Rhob Kerogen
parameters.note: index (64). VERBATIM: 'Density of Kerogen. Default is 1.1 gm/cc'

parameters.name: Nphi Kerogen
parameters.note: index (65). VERBATIM: 'Neutron of Kerogen. Default is 0.6 v/v'

parameters.name: Rhob Heavy_Min.
parameters.note: index (66). VERBATIM: 'Density of Heavy minerals associated with organic shale (mainly Pyrite). Default is 4.3 gm/cc'

parameters.name: Nphi Heavy_Min.
parameters.note: index (67). VERBATIM: 'Neutron of Heavy minerals associated with organic shale (mainly Pyrite). Default is -0.03 v/v'

parameters.name: Kerogen Wt%_Con.
parameters.note: index (68). VERBATIM: 'Conversion factor to convert input TOC curve, in weight %, to a volume curve. Default is 2.5'. 'If the input TOC curve is already in volume then set this factor to 1.0'

parameters.name: Heavy_Min. Wt%_Con.
parameters.note: index (69). VERBATIM: 'Conversion factor to convert input Heavy Mineral curve, in weight %, to a volume curve. Default is 1.0 (input is already in volumes).'

methods.equation: TEXT (recoverable, verbatim): GrCorr = Gr_in - TOC_in x Kerogen_Wt%Con x Gr_Kerogen ;; TOCvol = TOC_in x Kerogen_Wt%Con ;; HvyMinVol = HvyMin_in x HvyMin_Wt%Con ;; NeuCorr = (Neu_in - TOCvol x NeuKer ? HvyMinVol x NeuHvy) / (1.0 - TOCvol - HvyMinVol) ;; DenCorr = (Den_in - TOCvol x DenKer ? HvyMinVol x DenHvy) / (1.0 - TOCvol - HvyMinVol)
caveats: CHARACTER-MANGLING WARNING: the '?' in the NeuCorr and DenCorr numerators is a character that did not survive CHM decompilation. It is recorded as '?' and NOT silently resolved to a minus sign. Verify before implementing.
Corrected curves are always output when the feature is on; the per-zone flag only selects which curves Vcl consumes.
Corrected Vcl applies to 'Vclay Gamma Ray, Vclay Neutron and Vclay Neutron Density' only.
Input unit auto-detection: units of '%', 'pec' or 'wt%' -> divided by 100 to v/v; all other units assumed already v/v.
Heavy Mineral Volume input is optional; blank means heavy mineral volume = zero.

defaults_verbatim.statement: This allows the shape of the Stieber equation to be changed. Default is 2.0
STB = Stieber Constant shape parameter (default =2.0)

Numbers greater than 100% are allowed and are normal for the calculation of clay volume (default is 130%). Percentiles over 100% are calculated by a linear scaling from the 0% to the 100% percentiles and extrapolating to the entered number.
Numbers can be less than 0%. Negative percentiles are calculated by a linear scaling from the 0% to the 100% percentiles and extrapolating to the negative entered number.
The 'Clip Low %' and the 'Clip High %' parameters are used to eliminate spikes in the data which will artificially change the percentiles. Enter a low clip values between 0-100%. Default is (0%).
Enter a high clip values between 0-100%. Default is (98%).
Clip Low % : ... Enter a low clip values between 0-100%. Default is (98%). [CONFLICTS with clayparameters.htm which states 0% for Clip Low and 98% for Clip High]

The GammaRay curve data for each 'Percentile Group' is clipped using the 'Clip Low %' and the 'Clip High %' parameters before the percentiles are calculated. This allows a percentile of say 130% to be calculated with the removal of spikes in the data before the 130% is calculated.

The Percentile is calculated from the input GammRay curve data for all zones which have the same 'Percentile Group' number as the current zone. Hence if all zones use the same 'Percentile Group' number then a 10th percentile for all zones will give the same Gr Clean for all zones.
Hence if all zones use the same 'Percentile Group' number then a 90th percentile for all zones will give the same Gr Clay for all zones.
Density of Kerogen. Default is 1.1 gm/cc
Neutron of Kerogen. Default is 0.6 v/v
Density of Heavy minerals associated with organic shale (mainly Pyrite). Default is 4.3 gm/cc
Neutron of Heavy minerals associated with organic shale (mainly Pyrite). Default is -0.03 v/v
Conversion factor to convert input TOC curve, in weight %, to a volume curve. Default is 2.5
Conversion factor to convert input Heavy Mineral curve, in weight %, to a volume curve. Default is 1.0 (input is already in volumes).

If this is a new Run , then default parameters will be calculated for each clay indicator and these values will populate the Clay Volume Parameters Set. These defaults are not meant to be the optimum interpretation parameters, but are chosen simply to set the parameters within the correct range of values for a particular single curve or pair of curves.
For the Single Clay Indicators the defaults are generally the maximum and minimum readings for the indicator.

For the Double Clay Indicators the defaults will be the sandstone line for the clean line , and the shale point will be chosen towards the bottom right hand edge of the shale points , as seen on a standard crossplot.

Gr Clean : Gamma Ray clean value. Used for calculating Clay Volume. Should be set to the minimum Gamma Ray value seen in clean (non shaley) intervals. This defaults to the minimum Gamma Ray value seen in the Gamma Ray input curve.

Gr Clay : Gamma Ray clay value. Used for calculating Clay Volume. Should be set to the maximum Gamma Ray value seen in shale intervals. This defaults to the maximum Gamma Ray value seen in the Gamma Ray input curve.

NOTE: When setting the Neu Clean Parameter, exercise caution if setting this parameter to any other value than zero. This indicator can easily under-estimate the clay volume if the parameter is set too high.
Value of the resistivity in a clean, zero Vclay zone. Generally chosen as the highest resistivity in a hydrocarbon-bearing, clay-free zone.
Rho Matrix : Matrix density of the clean rock. ... Defaults to 2.65 gm/cc for sandstone. Set to 2.71 gm/cc for limestone.
Rho Fluid : Density of the fluid in the rock. ... Defaults to 1.0 gm/cc for fresh water. Set to 1.1 gm/cc for salt water.
Rho Clay : ... The default value is chosen as the maximum density reading over the interval where the sonic is high.
DT Matrix : Sonic matrix transit time of the clean rock. ... Defaults to 55 uSec/ft for sandstone. Set to 49 uSec/ft for limestone.
DT Fluid : Sonic fluid transit time in the rock. ... Default value is189 uSec/ft. For salt-saturated formation water use about 174 usec/ft.

Sonic Cp : Wyllie equation compaction factor. ... Defaults to 1.0. For unconsolidated sands this needs to be increased. A rule of thumb for estimating this parameter is to divide the sonic clay parameter by 100. The result should be greater than 1.0 for a valid Cp value.
Sat Equation : Water Saturation equation. Defaults to Archie.
Rw : Formation water resistivity at formation temperature. Defaults to 0.1 ohmm but must be adjusted to the correct value.
a factor : Archie equation a factor. Defaults to 1.0.
m Exponent : Archie equation m (cementation) factor. Defaults to 2.0.
n Exponent : Archie equation n (saturation exponent) factor. Defaults to 2.0.
The default porosity method is Density unless only the Sonic curve has been enter in which case the program will select the Sonic method for porosity.

It is recommended that the Raymer equation is used by default since this equation automatically takes care of the problem of unconsolidated sands, whilst the Wyllie equation has an extra compaction factor parameter which has to be estimated.
If the Bad Hole indicator logic is used, then over any interval which is flagged as Bad Hole all the Double Clay Indicators will be set to Null (-999).
for Z less than 0.55 [EQUATION IMAGE] / for Z greater than 0.55 and less than 0.73 [EQUATION IMAGE] / for Z greater than 0.73 and less than 1.0 VclGr = Z

terminology.ip_position: A module-level mode switch made BEFORE running, not a relabel. Verbatim: 'Before running this module a fundamental decision has to be made whether you which to calculate Clay volume or Shale volume. The module has been designed for clay volumes. But can be used just as easily for Shale volume calculations.'
terminology.consequences_stated: 'When selected the window labels, output curves and parameter names will adjust appropriately. Note changing this selection on a current parameter set will not change any of the parameter values currently used, it will be up to the user to re-pick the parameters for the type of analysis. However the default output curve names will change. This could mean the wrong input Vcl or Vsh curve could be used in the PhiSw module.'

terminology.term: Shale as a rock type (a mixture), clay as a mineral volume
terminology.ip_position: Verbatim: 'Shales normally contain 50-80% of clay. The actual clay contain could change at each depth level and is why shales are usually seen as a cloud of points on crossplot.'
terminology.consequences_stated: 'It is clearly easier to pick shale points than clay points, however it must be remembered that the porosity analysis modules work volumetrically and can only handle mineral volumes e.g. clay volume. If shale volumes are picked these have to be converted to clay volume before they can be used correctly.'

terminology.term: Shale pick vs clay pick (crossplot picking convention)
terminology.ip_position: Verbatim: 'Shale picks are normally made to the edge of the cloud of points while clay picks are made outside the cloud to give around 60-80% clay content.'
terminology.consequences_stated: Named pick types listed on the page: 'N/D Shale point pick', 'N/D Clay point pick', 'Gamma Ray Shale pick', 'Gamma Ray Clay Pick'.

terminology.term: Clay Shale Ratio (CSR) - the Vsh<->Vcl bridge
terminology.ip_position: Verbatim (swparameters.htm): '(178) Clay Shale Ratio ? the percentage of clay in 100% shale in decimals (v/v). Used to calculate the clay parameters from the shale parameters or vice versa. Also used to calculate the final Vshale output from the VWCL curve. Vshale = VWCL / CSR'. Also (swequationsandmethodology.htm): 'CSR = input Clay Shale Ratio parameter ( The fraction of clay seen in 100% shale ).'
terminology.consequences_stated: Endpoint conversions stated in text: 'Rho Wet Clay = Rho Matrix + ((Rho Shale - Rho Matrix) / CSR)'; 'Neu Wet Clay = Neu Matrix + ((Neu Shale - Neu Matrix) / CSR)'; 'Son Wet Clay = Son Matrix + ((Son Shale - Son Matrix) / CSR)'. NO DEFAULT VALUE FOR CSR IS STATED ON ANY PAGE READ.

terminology.ip_position: VCL = minimum of all selected indicators and by default becomes VWCL (Wet Clay Volume) into the PhiSw module. VCLAV = average (Mean|Median|Lateral). VCLMIX = per-zone selection of Minimum or Average.
terminology.consequences_stated: 'The Minimum Clay Volume ( VCL ) curve is calculated as the minimum clay volume response of all selected single and double clay indicators, and, by default is picked as the Wet Clay Volume ( VWCL ) curve used in the set up of the Porosity and Water Saturation Module.'

terminology.term: Per-indicator QC curves are deliberately unclipped
terminology.ip_position: Verbatim: 'The curve results for these indicators will not be limited to between 0 and 1.0. These curves are meant for quality control purposes, and should not be used in another module for Vclay, unless they are clipped first to between 0 and 1.0.'
terminology.consequences_stated: 'Vclay minimum ( VCL )and Vclay average ( VCLAV ) curves will also be calculated. These curves are clipped to between 0 and 1.0. For the VCLAV curve, the separate Vclay indicator curves will first be clipped before the average curve is created.' -> CLIP EACH INDICATOR FIRST, THEN AVERAGE.

terminology.term: Neutron curves are always assumed limestone matrix units
terminology.ip_position: Verbatim: 'IP makes the assumption that any neutron curve entered is in Limestone matrix units . If this is not the case, then the curve should be converted to Limestone porosity units using the appropriate service company environmental correction module or the Basic Log Analysis Functions module.'
terminology.consequences_stated: Restated on clayparameters.htm and basicloganalysis.htm. Also: 'all Neutron tools are calibrated to read correctly in limestone'.

terminology.ip_position: Verbatim: 'If the units are set at '%', 'pec' or 'wt%' then the input curve will be assumed to be in units of percent and will be divided by 100 to get it in units of ?v/v?. All other units will be assumed to be ?v/v?.'
terminology.consequences_stated: A unit-string whitelist, not a magnitude heuristic - worth copying as a pattern, but the whitelist is short and case handling is unstated.

terminology.term: Bad Hole 'Min' is an upper gate and 'Max' is a lower gate
terminology.ip_position: Verbatim: 'When the Bad Hole Indicator 1 curve values are greater than this minimum value , any double clay indicators will be switched off.' / '...less than this maximum value , any double clay indicators will be switched off.'
terminology.consequences_stated: Confirmed operationally on clayplot.htm: 'Set the BadH1 Min parameter to the maximum allowable caliper value'. Counter-intuitive naming - a direct reimplementation trap.

terminology.ip_position: Both clayparameters.htm and clayequationsandmethodology.htm use 'Stieber' consistently, including the parameter name 'Stieber Constant'.
terminology.consequences_stated: Relevant for parameter-name matching when reading IP parameter sets or .par files.

terminology.term: Lithology curve = flag curve + external index map
terminology.ip_position: Verbatim: 'Lithology Curves in IP are "flag" type curves with values mapped to Lithology Bitmaps (stored in Lithology.opt).'
terminology.consequences_stated: The index->lithology map is user-editable per project, so a LITH curve is meaningless without its accompanying Lithology.opt. Any importer must carry the map alongside the curve.

lithology_scheme.note: NOT stated in the manual - the manual only gives the count (39), the ordering rule (ascending alphabetic by description), the cap (80) and the bitmap size (16x16 px). The mappings below were read READ-ONLY from the shipped config file; nothing was written to the IP install.
lithology_scheme.format: index,BitmapName,Description (3-column CSV, one per line, 39 rows)
structural_observations: Flat list with modifier suffixes (- sandy, - muddy, - calc., - arg., - silty, - tuff., - volc., - carb., - ark., - fine), not a hierarchy.
Indices carry no numeric/petrophysical semantics - index 5 (Chalk) is not 'between' 4 and 6 in any physical sense.

Ordering is alphabetical by description, which is why index 36 (Siltstone) precedes 37 (Shale) - the sort is on 'Siltstone' vs 'Shale'... actually SLTST/Siltstone at 36 before SHALE/Shale at 37 breaks strict alphabetical order; recorded as-is from the file.
Both 'Clay' (8) and 'Claystone' (9) and 'Shale' (37) exist as separate entries - IP keeps the clay/claystone/shale distinction at the lithology level too.

These are also used by the Porosity and Water Saturation module.' (basiclogcalculations.htm); 'The Timur , Morris Biggs oil and Morris Biggs gas defaults come from the Western Atlas chartbook, whilst the Schlumberger Chart K3 is from the Schlumberger chartbook.'; 'Sigma Water is calculated using the charts in the Schlumberger chart book (Tcor-2a and Tcor-3b).'; 'Sigma Oil is calculated from GOR using charts in the Western Atlas chart book (8-6 Rev1 12-95 chart book).'; 'Sigma Gas is calculated using the Schlumberger chart for Methane (Tcor-1). This is the largest 'looks like Tier A, is not' trap in target B.
